failures.triage_note: With site currency set to EUR, the listing card / listing detail / JSON-LD all correctly rendered EUR (priceCurrency:"EUR" confirmed in three places in the rendered page source, listing and directory card prices all showed €). But the dashboard Credits tab's Buy Credits pack list showed the WooCommerce-backed '50 Credit Pack' as $25.00 (hardcoded/WooCommerce-store-currency, WooCommerce's own woocommerce_currency option stayed USD) side-by-side with the direct/Stripe-backed 'Stripe Test Pack' correctly showing €9.99. The runbook explicitly names 'the credit-packs screen' as one of the four surfaces that must agree, and it did not — a member sees two different currency symbols on the same screen. Root cause is architectural: the WooCommerce-adapter pack is a real WC product whose price/currency IS what WooCommerce will actually charge at checkout, so relabeling its displayed currency without changing what WC charges would be worse (a promise the checkout does not keep); the direct/Stripe adapter correctly reads wb_listora_get_setting('currency'). The fix likely belongs on the WooCommerce-adapter pack's own currency source (mirror the site setting into the WC product, or badge the pack with its real charge currency) rather than the shared display formatter Free's D-row assumes exists.
failures.expected: The SAME currency symbol/code renders on the listing card, listing detail price, credit-packs screen, and JSON-LD offers.priceCurrency after a site currency change.
failures.actual: Credit-packs screen shows $25.00 for the WooCommerce-backed pack and €9.99 for the direct/Stripe-backed pack simultaneously, while listing card/detail/JSON-LD all correctly show €.
failures.url: http://listora.local/my-listings/?tab=credits (as credituser, site currency temporarily set to EUR then restored to USD)

failures.triage_note: src/blocks/user-dashboard/view.js:707 (refreshCreditsBalanceAfterCheckout -> tryFetch) calls fetch('/wp-json/wbcom-credits/v1/wb-listora', ...) — the bare namespace root with no leaf route. The actual balance route registered is /wbcom-credits/v1/wb-listora/balance (confirmed via GET /wp-json/ route list). Every poll attempt 404s (rest_no_route), reproduced live: navigating to the post-checkout success URL produced two console errors for exactly that malformed URL. claimOnce() at the same file (line 685) correctly posts to /claim/{gateway} and is unaffected. Net effect: the banner correctly says 'Payment received. Adding N credits…' (this session's other fix, confirmed working) but the balance line below it can never confirm client-side — after 10 failed 3s polls it always falls through to 'Your credits will appear shortly — refresh in a moment if not.' even when the claim/webhook already succeeded server-side. A hard page refresh shows the correct new balance; only the live client-side confirmation is broken. One-line fix: append '/balance' to the fetch URL.
failures.expected: tryFetch() polls the real balance endpoint and the banner's balance line updates in-page once the claim/webhook lands, per the commit that introduced claimOnce() as 'the return path is now self-sufficient.'
failures.actual: tryFetch() always 404s against the wrong URL; the balance line never self-updates and always degrades to the 30-second timeout message.

failures.triage_note: bin/architecture-checks.sh (Pro, run live this session) INV-14 requires 100% token-based admin CSS. Two files carry a raw hex literal as the innermost fallback of a var() chain: assets/css/admin/settings.css:349 and the generated assets/css/admin/settings-rtl.css:349, both `background: var(--listora-surface, var(--listora-wp-admin-bg, #fff));`. Both files are inside this release's settings-CSS rewrite (commits 'Settings labels get their gap' / 'Selects stop clipping their own text; RTL twins are generated, not remembered' etc, ~1000-line settings-rtl.css diff). Low customer impact (the fallback only fires if both custom properties are undefined, which does not happen on a normal WP admin load) but it is a genuine, reproducible architecture-gate failure on code this release touched, not a pre-existing one — flagging per the release-gate checklist in CLAUDE.md which requires this script to return 0 before tagging.
